summary:
Johor is one of thirteen Malaysian state jurisdictions and stands under the national framework: the federal Penal Code applies in full within its borders, and Johor maintains its own Sharia enactment binding on Muslims. The substance of both layers is set out in the national assessment.

In November 2023 the Johor state government announced plans to establish conversion-therapy centres to "rehabilitate" LGBT people. The announcement is a formal statement of policy by the state administration rather than a criminal provision, and it is the clearest documented expression of official hostility from this state's government in the record.

The conversion-therapy announcement sits within a national pattern of state-conducted "rehabilitation" programmes: at least 1,733 people had attended such programmes as of June 2021, under a crackdown running since the 2018 election. Human Rights Watch and Justice for Sisters' state-conducted investigations, published 10 August 2022, covered Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Kelantan, Penang, Pahang and Kedah; Johor was not among the states investigated in that reporting, so no Johor-specific enforcement incident is documented in this record.
tangentialFactors:
The federal Penal Code sections 377A-377D, which criminalise same-sex intimacy and "outrages on decency" with up to twenty years' imprisonment with whipping for both men and women, apply in Johor as everywhere in Malaysia; the Human Dignity Trust profile of 16 December 2025 restates this alongside Johor's Sharia layer. Sharia enactments prohibit cross-dressing and "males posing as females", and state Sharia laws criminalise same-sex intimacy for Muslims.

Johor's November 2023 conversion-therapy announcement aligns the state with the federal religious-affairs posture documented nationally, in which government-funded "rehabilitation" retreats and conversion therapy are promoted by officials rather than merely tolerated.
localsOnly:
Johor's own Sharia enactment binds Muslim residents on cross-dressing and same-sex conduct, enforced by the state Islamic religious department; the federal Penal Code additionally binds all residents regardless of religion. Muslim residents in Johor are also subject to the 1982 National Fatwa Council position on sex reassignment, as described in the national record.

The state government's November 2023 policy statement commits Johor to operating conversion-therapy centres, a resident-facing service posture with no equivalent documented for visitors.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Johor-specific enforcement incident, arrest, raid or prosecution against a trans or gender-nonconforming person is documented in this inventory; the record contains only the state's 2023 policy announcement. Whether the announced conversion-therapy centres have been established and are operating is unresolved in these sources.

The inventory does not state whether Johor's Sharia enactment contains a provision on "women posing as males" in addition to the male cross-dressing provision, nor whether Johor has a counselling or rehabilitation order provision of the kind documented for Kelantan, Pahang and Terengganu.
